sections.content: You know the participle clause (*Terminada la reunión, salimos*) from B2 Unit 35. A method uses it to link its steps: each one starts from the result of the one before. *Obtenida la masa, se deja reposar* means "Once the dough is obtained, it is left to rest." The noun comes after the participle, and the participle agrees with it in gender and number like an adjective, because the meaning is passive: the dough has been obtained. The main clause is often a step with *se*, as in the earlier lesson of this unit.

sections.title: Steps in order
rows: Once the ingredients are measured, they are mixed.
Obtenida la masa, se deja reposar.
Once the dough is obtained, it is left to rest.
Horneado el pan, se deja enfriar.
Once the bread is baked, it is left to cool.
Una vez enfriada la masa, se amasa de nuevo.
Once the dough has cooled, it is kneaded again.

sections.content: Match the participle with the noun that follows it: *obtenida la masa*, *obtenidos los datos*. Keep the order participle + noun; *una vez* before the clause makes the "once" meaning clearer, but then no *que*: *una vez enfriado el pan*, not *una vez que enfriado el pan*. When the same person does both steps, *después de* + an infinitive (A2 Unit 4) also works; the participle clause is best when the thing, not the person, is what matters.
